messages.owner: Add a CSV export to the customers page
messages.reply:
I queued the task "Add CSV export to the customers page" under the Customer screens goal. No thread has picked it up yet.

What the brief asks for:
- **Download link:** `GET /customers.csv` downloads a file named `customers.csv`. An "Export CSV" link goes on `/customers`.
- **Columns:** Name, VAT and Created. Created uses DD/MM/YYYY, the date rule from the notebook.
- **File safety:**
  - Commas, quotes and line breaks inside fields are handled so the file opens correctly.
  - Names starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` get a leading quote so spreadsheets don't run them as formulas.
  - A marker at the start of the file lets Excel show accented names correctly.
- **Tests:** unit tests for the CSV content, plus a browser test that clicks the link and checks the downloaded file.
- **Report:** the thread must send back the pull request link and a sample of the CSV.

The notebook is updated with this plan.

No open questions.

{"title":"Add CSV export to the customers page","brief":"Owner request: "Add a CSV export to the customers page."

Context
- Node 20 + TypeScript app. Customers store: src/customers/index.ts (Customer = { id, name, vat, createdAt ISO string }, persisted in $SANDBOX_DATA_DIR/customers.json). Web server: src/web/server.ts renders /customers as an HTML table (Name, VAT) and serves /api/customers as JSON. Unit tests use vitest (src/**/index.test.ts); browser tests use Playwright (tests/browser/customers.spec.ts). Follow AGENTS.md (never run scripts/owner-only.sh).
- Project rule: dates shown to users are always DD/MM/YYYY.

What to build
1. A CSV serializer for customers (put it in src/customers, pure function, unit tested). Columns: Name, VAT, Created (createdAt formatted DD/MM/YYYY). Header row first. RFC 4180 quoting: wrap fields containing comma, double quote, CR or LF in double quotes and double any inner quotes. Use CRLF line endings. Guard against CSV formula injection: prefix fields starting with =, +, -, @, tab or CR with a single quote. Prepend a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens non-ASCII names correctly.
2. A download route, e.g. GET /customers.csv (make sure the existing /customers startsWith match does not swallow it), responding with Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8 and Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="customers.csv". Empty store returns only the header row.
3. A visible "Export CSV" link/button on the /customers page pointing at the route. Text label only, no emoji. Keep it visually consistent with the existing page.

Tests
- Vitest: serializer covers header, DD/MM/YYYY date, quoting of commas/quotes/newlines, formula-injection prefixing, empty list.
- Playwright: on /customers, the Export CSV control is visible; clicking it triggers a download named customers.csv whose content starts with the header and includes a seeded customer.
- Run lint/typecheck, vitest and Playwright; all green. Fix any pre-existing failure you hit.

Done when: the export works end to end in a browser, tests pass, CHANGELOG.md has an entry, and the PR is open.
